prayerExcerpt.en-US: Every Christian ought, by his manner, to bear witness to the sanctity of his faith.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Todo cristão deveria, por seu modo de viver, dar testemunho da santidade de sua fé.

meta.face: A Roman of about fifty with a fair olive complexion and a BROAD, SHORT, ROUND-JAWED face like an Antonine portrait bust — a wide, low forehead with the hair growing forward on it, full, rounded cheeks, a SHORT, THICK, straight nose, LARGE, slightly PROMINENT eyes under HEAVY, half-lowered upper lids, giving the dreamy, thoughtful look of the portraits of his day, soft, level brown brows, a small, full mouth; thick, dark-brown hair in short, crisp curls, a SHORT, close, curly dark-brown beard trimmed to the line of the round jaw; the gaze calm and inward, a little to the side.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; Wikipedia's lead image shows another Apollonius. The Roman Martyrology (quoted on Wikipedia) calls him 'philosopher and martyr', who defended the faith before the Prefect Perennis and the Senate under Commodus; the book makes him a senator versed in philosophy and Scripture, and its engraving shows him in a toga before a seated Roman. The card follows the book's rank (the broad stripe) and the fashion of Antonine portraits for the short curly beard and heavy-lidded eyes. The broad, short, round-jawed face is our choice, apart from `justin`, the other philosopher-martyr.
